nodes.description: Progressive central nervous system dysfunction arising from neuronal sphingomyelin storage manifests after infancy with variable neurological signs—particularly cerebellar ataxia, gross motor developmental delay, and learning difficulties—distinguishing chronic neurovisceral ASMD (NPD-A/B) from non-neuronopathic NPD-B.

nodes.description: Olipudase alfa (recombinant human acid sphingomyelinase) is FDA-approved for the non-CNS (visceral and pulmonary) manifestations of ASMD across subtypes; because it does not cross the blood-brain barrier, it reduces liver, spleen, and lung sphingomyelin storage without impacting CNS neurocognitive or motor manifestations in NPD-A/B.

evidence.reference_title: Acid Sphingomyelinase Deficiency.
evidence.snippet: Olipudase alfa (Xenpozyme®) enzyme replacement therapy (ERT) helps to reduce the accumulation of sphingomyelin in the lung, liver, spleen, and other non-central nervous system organs. It does not impact the central nervous system and therefore does not impact the neurocognitive issues seen in individuals with NPD-A or NPD-A/B.

evidence.reference_title: The Genetic Basis, Lung Involvement, and Therapeutic Options in Niemann-Pick Disease: A Comprehensive Review.
evidence.snippet: Enzyme replacement therapy with Olipudase α is the first and only approved disease-modifying therapy for patients with ASMD.

nodes.description: Undegraded sphingomyelin and secondary lipids (cholesterol and gangliosides) accumulate in lysosomes of tissue macrophages (forming lipid-laden foam cells) and, to an intermediate degree, within central nervous system and retinal neurons, driving parallel visceral and neurologic pathology.

evidence.reference_title: Types A and B Niemann-Pick disease.
evidence.snippet: The eponym Niemann-Pick disease (NPD) refers to a group of patients who present with varying degrees of lipid storage and foam cell infiltration in tissues, as well as overlapping clinical features including hepatosplenomegaly, pulmonary insufficiency and/or central nervous system (CNS) involvement.

evidence.reference_title: Types A and B Niemann-Pick disease.
evidence.snippet: The principal accumulating lipid is sphingomyelin, but cholesterol and ganglioside storage also has been observed.

nodes.description: Progressive interstitial lung disease from pulmonary storage macrophages.

evidence.reference_title: Disease manifestations and burden of illness in patients with acid sphingomyelinase deficiency (ASMD).
evidence.snippet: Almost all patients have hepatosplenomegaly and an atherogenic lipid profile, and most patients have interstitial lung disease with progressive impairment of pulmonary function and hematologic abnormalities including cytopenias.

nodes.description: Later-onset and highly variable central nervous system manifestations (ranging from mild to severe neurologic symptoms) distinguish chronic neurovisceral ASMD (NPD-A/B) from non-neuronopathic NPD-B.

nodes.description: Biallelic SMPD1 variants leave low intermediate residual acid sphingomyelinase activity (<10% of normal controls): higher than in infantile neurovisceral NPD-A, preventing rapid infantile psychomotor collapse, yet insufficient for normal sphingomyelin turnover in macrophages and vulnerable central nervous system neurons.

evidence.reference_title: Types A and B Niemann-Pick disease.
evidence.snippet: All patients with types A and B NPD have mutations in the gene encoding ASM (SMPD1), and thus the disease is more accurately referred to as ASM deficiency (ASMD).

evidence.reference_title: Acid Sphingomyelinase Deficiency.
evidence.snippet: The diagnosis of ASMD is established by detection of biallelic pathogenic variants in SMPD1 by molecular genetic testing and residual acid sphingomyelinase enzyme activity that is less than 10% of controls (in peripheral blood lymphocytes or cultured skin fibroblasts).
